text:
Alex Kim: FYI customer (AcmePay) opened an escalation — their batch rerank answers are getting candidates mixed between queries. They included a minimized repro, failing in prod 2/3 times.

Maya Singh: Oof. Can you paste the exact request/response and the request-id?

Alex Kim: Request-id: req_0a7c9f3d. Repro payload they used (sanitized):
```json
{
  "queries": ["how to refund a payment", "chargeback policy for merchants"],
  "candidates": [
    [
      {"id": "c1", "text": "refund flow"},
      {"id": "c2", "text": "refund timeline"}
    ],
    [
      {"id": "c3", "text": "chargeback steps"},
      {"id": "c4", "text": "merchant disputes"}
    ]
  ]
}
```
And their observed response (excerpt):
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"query_index": 0, "ranked_candidate_ids": ["c3", "c4"], "scores": [0.9, 0.85]},
    {"query_index": 1, "ranked_candidate_ids": ["c1", "c2"], "scores": [0.88, 0.82]}
  ]
}
```
Which obviously looks like the candidate lists got swapped across the two queries. They said it happens intermittently (2/3 attempts) and only with batched multi-query requests, single-query rerank works fine.

Jordan Lee: Do we have the server logs for req_0a7c9f3d? Any correlation ids?

Support Bot: (automated) Correlation / trace: trace=trace-9c12, host=node-17a.redwood.prod; logs attached to ticket INC-7138.

Alex Kim: Pasted a small chunk of server debug we got back (redacted):
```text
[2026-02-12T14:03:21Z] INFO incoming batch size=2 candidates_total=4 request_id=req_0a7c9f3d
[2026-02-12T14:03:21Z] DEBUG flattening candidates -> flat_candidates_len=4
[2026-02-12T14:03:21Z] DEBUG compute offsets -> offsets=[0,2]
[2026-02-12T14:03:21Z] DEBUG scoring loop i in range(4) using global_index for candidate-> assigns scores to query_index = floor(global_index / ???)
[2026-02-12T14:03:21Z] ERROR mismatch detected: assigned_query_index out_of_bounds for some candidates
```

Maya Singh: That log line stands out — "using global_index for candidate-> assigns scores to query_index = floor(global_index / ???)". Sounds like the runtime might be partitioning by a fixed chunk size rather than using the computed per-query offsets. If some internal batching/worker size changes, it could misassign.

Jordan Lee: Hypothesis: somewhere in the path we flatten candidates into a single list and then rely on a constant stride to reconstruct per-query buckets. If candidate counts per query vary, stride-based reconstruction will misalign.

ML OnCall Bot: (automated) ML model runner version: v2.3.1; serving-runtime: inferd-1.8.4. Known related fix: inferd PR#425 addresses per-query offset mapping in a different codepath (not yet in prod).

Maya Singh: Repro steps I used locally: 1) send the same payload w/ 2 queries (2 candidates each), 100x loop, 2) enable debug logging on server, 3) watch results. I can reproduce ~40% locally when running on node-17a config.

Alex Kim: Customer also reported a variant where queries had different candidate counts (query0 had 3, query1 had 1) and the server returned an index error once. So both misalignment and OOB possible.

Jordan Lee: Short-term mitigation: validate on API layer that the length of candidates arrays equals queries length, and if not exact, reject with 400 and an explanatory message. Also enforce a per-batch max_total_candidates limit to keep flatten logic safe. I can open a quick patch to add validation.

Maya Singh: Agreed, add strict validation + explicit offsets in the request/response would make things robust. For immediate customer unblock, we can run a transformation in the gateway: attach a "per_query_counts" field so downstream knows boundaries. But that is extra surface area.

Alex Kim: I told the customer a workaround: split into separate per-query requests until we ship a patch. They asked about latency/cost hit — they said it's acceptable short-term.

Jordan Lee: I'm going to bisect recent runtime deploys. If inferd PR#425 is not yet in prod, that may explain intermittent nature. Also check if worker shard size changed last week (eng-runtime release notes).

Maya Singh: For the fix: don't rely on uniform stride. Use the explicit offsets array computed from candidates lengths (we already log offsets, but code path must use that instead of stride). I'll write a unit test reproducing uneven candidate lists, plus a fuzz test that randomizes per-query sizes.

ML OnCall Bot: (automated) Incident created: INC-7138. Severity: P2. Assigned teams: eng-runtime, eng-ml, support.

Jordan Lee: I'll draft the change and push to canary today. Alex, can you coordinate a smoke test with AcmePay once canary is up?

Alex Kim: Yep — will coordinate. Also asked for timeline: can we target a hotfix within 48 hours?

Jordan Lee: Aiming for a hotfix PR + canary <48h. If the validation mitigation lands earlier, we can disable batching for the affected tenant as a fallback.

Maya Singh: Notes for the rollout doc: - Add API validation error: "candidates must be an array of arrays matching queries length" - Add telemetry to surface batch misalignments (metrics: rerank.batch.misaligned_count) - Postmortem checklist: identify any customers who used mixed-length candidate batches in last 30d.

Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. I'll update the customer and paste their acceptance steps here after the smoke test. :thumbsup:

Support Bot: (automated) Ticket INC-7138 updated: priority P2, linked to PR#6721, canary pipeline started.

ML OnCall Bot: (automated) Closing note: if anyone sees additional similar traces, add a comment to INC-7138 and tag @eng-runtime.
